study type: Retrospective cohort study with historical comparison
exposure: Therapeutic hypothermia treatment for intrapartum asphyxia
outcome: Cerebral palsy (overall, mild vs severe phenotype)
Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) scores
cohort: The study included all children treated with therapeutic hypothermia for intrapartum asphyxia in a single-center tertiary-level neonatal intensive care unit from 2008 to 2018 who developed cerebral palsy.
finding: In children with cerebral palsy treated with therapeutic hypothermia, there were more cases of spastic quadriparesis and epilepsy, and fewer visual impairments compared to a historical cohort; within the hypothermia cohort, higher birth weight, lower 5- and 10-minute Apgar scores, and specific MRI findings were significantly associated with a severe cerebral palsy phenotype.
birth_weight: Higher mean birth weight was found in the severe cerebral palsy group compared to the mild cerebral palsy group within the cooled cohort.
